correctness.rationale: Over an algebraic closure, degree-five del Pezzo has exactly ten exceptional curves, whose Petersen graph has twelve five-cycles. The embedded exact checker reproduces these, and all five boundary divisor classes form an integral Picard basis. Twisting by D5 gives exactly four Frobenius conjugacy types over finite fields, distinguished into S5 cycle types identity, 5-cycle, and double transposition. The complete surface Grothendieck classes follow from explicit smooth blowup/blowdown constructions, including one closed quintic orbit on a conic and two quadratic orbits, which exist for every finite q. Boundary normalization and its degree-ten incidence etale set yield [D]=(L+1)[V]-[B]+[E]. Subtracting the matched expressions gives the two unlocalized K0 classes. Cohomology follows from the determinant-one Picard basis, the localization sequence and graph orientation. The finite checker reproduces 120 oriented cycles, all ten D5 actions through twenty extension powers, exact small-field counts, and formal scissor identities; it is corroboration rather than proof of infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The asserted new claim is the exact integral Grothendieck-ring formula uniformly for all four marked finite-field pentagon types and all finite characteristics. Harpaz 2015 already classifies D5 geometric/Galois pair types in characteristic 0, gives the integral Picard basis, explicitly proves the H_c² orientation character (Proposition 3.2.8), and gives split and quadratic affine models; all are prior. Banwait--Fite--Loughran 2016 covers proper-surface Frobenius trace, and Boitrel 2023 covers degree-five arithmetic blowup forms; neither inspected paper states the exact K0 class of the nonproper pentagon complement. The formula is not regarded as an original first isolated finite-field point count or an original cohomology character. The new work requires constructing the S5-form surface K0 classes and finite-etale flag correction for all D5 boundary forms, not just applying an existing numerical count. Priority remains qualified because a specialist A2 cluster/motivic source might cover the same identity.
residual_risks: A specialist motivic study of cluster A2 surfaces or finite-field del Pezzo boundary complements might imply the same K0 identities under a different name.
Harpaz explicit split/quadratic affine models supply K0 calculations for their special cases with short extra arguments; those parts have not been asserted as novel in isolation.

The prime-field characteristic-two case is proved by general twisting and scissors rather than direct enumeration of every compactification; all-char proof depends on the standard Aut(Y)=S5 classification.

value.rationale: The deleted geometric pentagon is a canonical anticanonical log K3 boundary, and the D5 Galois character is its natural classification invariant. Determining the unlocalized Grothendieck class for every finite-field form is a complete, structural arithmetic classification not obtained merely from proper-surface zeta functions. It distinguishes orientation type but collapses four genuine marked classes to two, retaining a nontrivial etale degree-two term in the reflection case; exact point-count and compact-support cohomology are consequences. These are motivated invariants, not arbitrary small-field computations. Earlier numerical and cohomological special cases are disclosed as prior.
